txt: *"That's* the where you remember me from?"
*"That's* where you remember me from?"
Again he provides no reply, instead seemingly trying to get a better look of your attire through his sunglasses.
From within your mind-haze you hear the end of a sentence: "...and I'm not going to pretend like he's got a *learning disability*!"
He seems to be observing you through the reflective glass of his eye-wear. There's no reply. Perhaps repeat it?
Repeating it gets no reaction from the man with sunglasses. Suddenly the world is very quiet. Even the howling wind outside sounds a bit embarrassed.
The man doesn't reply. He's too busy furiously squinting at you.
The man in sunglasses nods.
The man with sunglasses looks at her -- then back at you: "Okay, superstar. Talk to me, what do you want? You want a pat on the back?"
"*Far Out* Son of Liver Failure -- the supercop who voluntarily enters an alcohol induced delirium to solve crimes."
"*You're* an asshole!" He pauses. "You know what, maybe we're both assholes..."
"... and the conclusion is that a man with your calibre should form his own one-man-policing-unit." He nods eagerly along. "Anyone else would just slow you down."
"...somewhere *good*."
"A cover-up -- where the author of the cover-up is the perp? Makes sense."
"A little premonition for you, lieutenant. Sooner or later -- probably sooner -- your new friend tells you he doesn't need you. He will then suggest you should *fuck off*."
"About *what?* You don't look like a cop..." He inspects you. "You know what you look like?"
"Actually, I *don't* want to hear you say things."
"Again?! I can't believe this shit..." He shakes his head, looking like he really is having trouble believing this *shit*.
"And I don't mean that as a metaphor."
"And you look like you don't bathe -- on principle," the man with sunglasses interjects.
"But as you're still staring at me like a calf stares at a freshly made gate... I assume there was something else."
"But you're not trying your best, are you?" He says with a flash of anger.
"Cause it's not my job. Why don't you go and fucking do yours and solve this damn hanging?"
"Cut the crazy act," the man with sunglasses interjects angrily. "She's being polite enough by not telling you to fuck off."
"Cut the shit." The words are addressed to you. "Every second you stand here running your mouth the case grows colder."
"Don't say anything, Judit."
"Exactly." The man nods excitedly in approval.
"Fucking *politics* again... You know what I'm more interested in?"
"Fucking deranged lunatic..." The sunglass-wearing man pushes through his teeth.
"Go ahead," he nods. "Have another guess."
"God fucking shit..." He pinches the root of his nose.
"Goddamnit, you leave her alone!" The man with sunglasses snaps at you. "Keep your weird bullshit to yourself and be professional for once, for fucks sake..."
"Good job, that was very close." He now speaks with the tone of a mother helping her kid take first steps. "Maybe try again?"
"Horrible, truly horrible," he continues. "I beg of you, don't ever subject anyone to this torture again. I mean seriously, you need to..."
"How about 41? How does 41st sound?" He shakes his head. "Never mind, I'm not going along with this..."
"I don't even know what to say to that..." he shakes his head. "What is your god damn station?"
"I don't know... why are you?" He gives you an odd look.
"I don't know..." He taps on his forehead, thinking. "A sad stack of shit?"
"I get it. Okay. But what is the motive?"
"I would love to -- but I'm busy *fucking off and not cramping your style*. And that might cramp it, you see. Helping you."
"I'm going to say... *no*. Just to see what you'll say to that. What do you say?"
"I'm sure he's fucking *flattered*, but *Kim* is not part of this thought experiment. In this one -- *we're* partners."
"If I wasn't clinically depressed, I'd burst out laughing." He doesn't look amused. "But I'm gonna go with *no* right now."
"It's not just this week." He scans you from head to toe. "What do you want?"
"Judit," He turns to the woman next to him. "Back me up here."
"Just some regular boring motherfuckers in suits and uniforms. Nothing spectacularly extravagant like you -- the Far Out Son Of Lung."
"Let's be crazy... let's say you and I are partners. How's that for a thought experiment?"
"Me? No. I'm just a man with sunglasses. I like wearing sunglasses inside. Sunglasses -- and a *fucking wig*."
"My condolences," the man with sunglasses replies dryly.
"NO ONE!" The man looks at her. "I'm just a man with sunglasses and you are..."
"NO!" The man in the sunglasses raises his fist. "You will not start blabbering about that asshole."
"Neither can I, partner. Neither can I..." His grey eyes suddenly flash above the glass frames. They feel sad.
"No!" he exclaims excitedly. "'Cause in this thought experiment we are police officers. In a police station. We don't do crimes -- we're not crime bros."
"No, Harry... it's *not* your name," the man scoffs. "Your name is Baron Von Kikkenberg -- cool guy."
"No, not entirely." It's impossible to say what his eyes behind the shades are doing.
"No, not like a revolutionary." He looks away.
"No, not really," he replies with the familiar fake enthusiasm. "Not really at all! Now *please* go sort this hanging out, alright?"
"No, not really." He let's the silence drag out.
"No," he says calmly, then just keeps staring at you.

"None taken, my friend -- none taken." He waves his hands. "Let's be honest, there's been some purely fictional talk in our imaginary station in regards of who'd even *be* worthy of your partnership..."
"Not as famous as you, superstar." He says without the slightest hint of irony.
"Not even a little bit."
"Not the prophet shit again..." He looks away.
"Nothing *works* for me, that's the problem, buddy." He closes his eyes and rubs his forehead. "Whatever, I don't really care."
"Now he's got a problem with learning disabilities... is that supposed to be ironic?"
"Now, what do you want?" His tone is impatient.
"Of course he does..." The man at the table says to himself.
"Oh don't be so modest, we're looking at several months' worth of damage here. Kind of a miracle you're still up and at it, to be honest..."
"Oh god, I'd hate for that to happen... you know what might help prevent that though?"
"Oh god... it's the fucking muscle thing..."
"Oh my god, there's more..." He looks at you in disbelief. "You want something more... what is it?"
"Oh no, NO, NO! You see, I enjoy watching other, better cops solve crimes -- and let me tell you, it's been quite a privilege seeing you work..."
"Oh really?! I wonder where?!"
"Oh yes, big time." He nods enthusiastically. "Who hasn't heard of the Far Out Son of Liver Failure?!"
"Oh you know me... always the joker -- just can't but see the bright side." He's doing a weird dance imitation with his elbows. "Guess I'm just pathologically a *glass is half-full* kind of guy."
"Oh, I definitely know you from *somewhere*."
"Oh, I wish I could, I wish I could..." he spreads his arms and shrugs. "Unfortunately I'm a neck and chin nurse. What you need is a head nurse. Sorry I couldn't help you out, buddy."
"Oh, it's you, you eccentric genius." He winks at you sarcastically. "I mean with your unorthodox approach to police work it *has to* be you."
"Oh, the Hypothetical Four-One. Yeah, let's *fantasize* about that." He blinks aggressively. "I'm not busy, you're not busy, let's just play around!"
"Oh, yes you are! And you've worked really, *really* hard, haven't you?"
"Oh, you're still here," he says, opening his eyes. "Must have had something really important for me?"
"Oh, you've done a lot more with ether than just *look into it*." He leans back and mumbles: "This was stupid, I shouldn't have..."
"Oh..." He seems taken aback for a moment. "Well, go solve your case then. That would count as *trying hard*."
"Okay then. It's probably a *coincidence*. People sound alike. Good bye."
"Okay, okay!" The man sounds genuinely excited. "That's plausible. That's entirely plausible. Now we're really getting somewhere..." He gives you a long, meaningful look and adds:
"Okay, why not. Let's do the whole thing over again. We're not wasting time. There *is* no time!"
"Okay. Say things." He adopts a lighter tone. "I want to hear you say things."
"Okay. Well..." He corrects his blonde wig. Khm... his hair. He corrects his hair.
"Okay... how about you stop wasting my time and get on with whatever you were doing then?"
"Okay?!"
"Or...OR..." The man with sunglasses raises his index finger. "We could go back to doing our jobs. This was stupid..."
"Perfect, great, I don't give a shit!" He shakes his head. "Now leave us alone and do your thing... and I don't mean get drunk and piss yourself, right? You realize that, don't you?"
"Seven years and going strong!" He nods enthusiastically. "The head doctors are now calling it a medical marvel... no, wait, anomaly was the word they used."
"So... do you know who hanged him?"
"Stupid is a gross understatement." You feel his eyes behind the shades mapping you out.
"Talk to me, superstar. What do you want?"
"That would be my first guess, yes."
"That's..." The man looks extremely surprised. "...exactly right! Down to a fraction."
"To what station do you think you would belong in this alternate and totally fictional reality?"
"To yourself -- yes, extremely."
"Uh, that was..." He stares at you. "Yeah, that was absolute shit -- if you want my opinion. Drunken shit. Haven't wanted anything to end this badly since I had cluster headaches."
"Watch out for yourself, loser!"
"Well that depends," the man with sunglasses says tilting his head. "Define *fire*."
"Well, I *am* interacting with the most dangerous animal of them all -- you -- I'd say yes. I'm animal control."
"Well, as far as disguises go, this is one of the best I've seen... I mean, I could swear you're an actual bum!"
"Well, he's not." The man interjects -- his voice is stern. "He's a sack of shit barely kept together by crazy glue -- but at least he tries. Unlike you."
"Well... where have you looked for her?"
"West of here? Though luck. The place is ruined from the bombardment. A lot of places to hide there..."
"What? No. Nonononono!" The man with sunglasses shakes his head stubbornly. "There are *universal* standards of good out there and that... that was just complete shit."
"What?"
"When that happens I suggest you take his advice," he adds bitterly.
"Why yes..." His eyes peer over the sunglasses. "Yes, I am a male nurse -- how could you tell?"
"Would you now?! Or would I be *cramping your style?*" The man bites his lip, then waves his hand. "Never mind... *partner*."
"Wow... You seem stable. And in control. Allow me to say, alcohol really seems to have had a positive effect on you."
"Yeaaah..." He's rubbing his chin as he drags out the *yeah*. "Sort of. Okay. I get the reference. Like after he got run over or something."
"Yeah, I can see that."
"Yeah, I know -- that's what I'm going by here."
"Yes sir, solving crimes, locking up bad guys and... *AND* get this... and *not* getting their drink on at two o'clock."
"Yes, and I'm wondering why? Don't you have a case to solve?"
"Yes. From another life. A different life. Maybe the life of a police officer belonging to the ranks of the..." He pauses.
"Yes. It's a hobby of mine." He looks at you inquisitively.
"Yes." He nods. "A superstar cop. Of course. *This* again."
"You doing your *fucking job*."
"You don't have a motive? Then the double cover-up seems too neat."
"You don't say?" He turns away from you. "Good bye then. The voice thing was a *coincidence*. Run along, asshole."
"You look like shit." Your ruffled face reflects in the man's sunglasses.
"You solving the case you're on." He takes a quick breath. "I'm passionate about that. So maybe -- get to it?"
"You think he was hanged as a coverup? To hide the shooting?"
"You think so?"
"You're not going to believe this, but..." The man pauses for dramatic effect. "... police officers!"
"You're not shitting me, Mullen. I can smell it all the way here. The whole town stinks."
"You're not. I really don't believe you are."
